title: refactor(service-automation): drop the redundant TryCatchErrorValue widening now that the spec declares `code`
body:
Fixes #15669

Clause-②: no

## What changed

Two lines of surface, in `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/try-catch-node.ts`:

1. `const errorValue: TryCatchErrorValue & { code?: string }` becomes `const errorValue: TryCatchErrorValue`.
2. The comment paragraph that began "`code` (#14419) is bound alongside but is NOT declared on `TryCatchErrorValueSchema`" is rewritten to state that the key **is** declared, pointing at the spec docblock that explains why the type stays open.

⛔ The object literal is untouched. `nodeId`, `message`, `code` and `iteration` / `item` are bound under exactly the same conditions, in the same order, as before. This is an observation-class card — a redundancy, not a defect — so the deliverable is the removal plus evidence that behaviour is unchanged, and the smallest correct diff is the right one.

## Why it is redundant

`TryCatchErrorValueSchema` declares `code: z.string().optional()`, so the exported `TryCatchErrorValue` already carries the member the local intersection was adding.

Re-verified on today's `origin/main` before anything was removed, with controls in both directions — the five declared keys read back as `nodeId` / `message` / `code` / `iteration` / `item`; two keys known not to be declared (`stackTrace`, `httpStatus`) read absent. So the presence of `code` is a real presence, not a mis-read schema.

## The redundancy proof (method: a throwaway type probe, deleted in the same turn)

A temporary file in the package's own tsc program, compiled by `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` against the freshly built spec `dist`:

| assertion | result |
|:---|:---|
| `TryCatchErrorValue['code']` is assignable to `string \| undefined` | holds |
| `string \| undefined` is assignable to `TryCatchErrorValue['code']` | holds |
| `TryCatchErrorValue` is assignable to the widened type | holds |
| the widened type is assignable to `TryCatchErrorValue` | holds |
| positive control — a type is assignable to itself | holds |
| **negative control** — `TryCatchErrorValue` assignable to `TryCatchErrorValue & { stackTrace: string }` (a REQUIRED undeclared key) | **reddens**, `TS2344` at the control's own line, nothing else |

tsc exit 0 with the five real assertions; exit 2 with the negative control added. The probe was live, so the five greens are readings.

⚠️ One honest nuance the card's wording does not carry: under TypeScript's **invariant type-identity** relation (the deferred-conditional `Equals` trick) the two are *not* the same type, because an intersection is never reduced to a single anonymous object type. Measured: that form reports `false`. What actually governs whether the annotation does anything is **mutual assignability** — the set of values it accepts and rejects — and that is identical, which is why the emit is byte-identical below. The card's "is then the same type" is true in the sense that matters and imprecise as type theory; no part of the deliverable changes either way.

## Evidence that nothing changed

**Package suite and typecheck, before and after:**

| | typecheck | test files | tests |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| before (`origin/main` base) | exit 0 | 135 passed (135) | 1599 passed (1599) |
| after (this branch) | exit 0 | 135 passed (135) | 1599 passed (1599) |

The AFTER leg ran as `build && typecheck && test` under the shared verify lock, so the wrapper's `VERDICT command-exit 0` covers all three. The BEFORE leg was sequenced with `;` and each part recorded its own exit code (`TYPECHECK_EXIT=0`, `TEST_EXIT=0`) — the wrapper printed `VERDICT batch-last-exit` for it and that number is deliberately not cited here.

`typecheck` really does cover this package's tests: `tsconfig.json`'s `include` is `["src"]` with no test exclusion, and `check:test-typecheck` reports the test layer compiling with `0 file(s) / 0 error(s)`.

**Published bytes, built both ways and compared file by file:**

| published file | before vs after |
|:---|:---|
| `dist/index.js` | byte-identical |
| `dist/index.cjs` | byte-identical |
| `dist/index.d.ts` | byte-identical |
| `dist/index.d.cts` | byte-identical |
| `dist/index.js.map` | differs by 1 byte |
| `dist/index.cjs.map` | differs by 1 byte |

The executable and type surfaces do not move at all. The two sourcemaps shift because the replacement comment is two lines longer and the map encodes line positions; the comment text itself reaches no published file (`check:sourcemap-no-sources-content` is why there is no `sourcesContent`, and a grep for the new and old comment text scores 0 in every published file, against a positive control that scores 10 in `index.js`).

That one-byte movement is also the whole reason this PR carries a **changeset** rather than `skip-changeset`: something published does move, however trivially, and that label is reserved for a diff that publishes nothing.

## Reverse verification — the PIN, not the fix

The interesting question for a no-op diff is whether the behaviour it calls "unchanged" is pinned at all. Mutation: delete `...(lastErrorCode ? { code: lastErrorCode } : {}),` from the catch-region binding, leaving the annotation in place.

On-disk proof before reading any result — anchor count 1 before, 0 after; blob `a24ef777…` (HEAD) became `65d8ee8a…`. The subject resolves through a **relative** specifier (`./try-catch-node.js`) from a test in the same package, so the operative artifact is the source file, not `dist`, and no dist preflight applies.

**It reddens, and precisely:**

```
Test Files  1 failed | 134 passed (135)
     Tests  2 failed | 1597 passed (1599)

FAIL src/builtin/create-record-duplicate-code.test.ts
  #14419 — a try_catch actually DISCRIMINATES … > swallows DUPLICATE_RECORD and takes the plain edge (not the fault edge)
  #14419 (PR #14948 patch round 1) … > loop over two rows: row 1 duplicate (swallowed), row 2 a timeout (must NOT inherit row 1's code)
```

Both failures are exactly the catch-region `code` discriminators — nothing incidental. Restored from `HEAD` afterwards and proven restored: blob back to `a24ef777…`, `git diff HEAD` empty. The mutation script carried a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` throughout.

## Clause-② re-derivation, from the delivered diff

Re-derived rather than inherited from the claim's prediction, on reachability from the published entry (`dist/index.js` / `dist/index.d.ts`), ⛔ not on the word `export`:

| probe | reading |
|:---|:---|
| positive control — `AutomationEngine` in the runtime entry | true |
| positive control — `installBuiltinNodes` in the runtime entry | true |
| positive control — `AutomationEngine` in `index.d.ts` | 49 occurrences |
| negative control — a name that exists nowhere | false |
| subject — `registerTryCatchNode` in the runtime entry | **false** (reached only through `installBuiltinNodes`) |
| subject — `TryCatchErrorValue` in `index.d.ts` | **0 occurrences** |
| subject — `errorValue` in the runtime entry | false (a function-local `const`) |
| runtime export list, pre-change vs delivered | identical, 28 names both ways |

No new exported symbol, no new key on a published payload, no published surface moves in either direction — and the mechanical floor for an automatic `yes` is exactly those two things. ⇒ **`Clause-②: no`**, now measured.

For completeness: `scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs --declaration no` exits 0 on this diff but reports the path as **NOT MEASURED** ("no declared surface covers it"), so it is not evidence in either direction and the determination above does not rest on it.

## Gates — the denominator

Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (its own header confirms: derived from `objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `f68a5abe6`, change set from the merge base `b3b43b6ea`, three-dot), then reconciled with `--ran` carrying an exit code per line:

```
Run reconciliation — 56 derived, 55 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
```

- **55 run green** (exit 0), including `check:nul-bytes`, `check:published-files`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:dts-closure`, `check-empty-changeset`, `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-adr-0087-registration`.
- **1 NOT MEASURED** — `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exits **3**, `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`: it reads built output and 49 packages in this worktree have no `dist/` (only the subject's dependency closure was built). ⛔ Not a pass and ⛔ not a red — nothing was measured. It needs a whole-repo `pnpm build`, which is CI's run. Its verdict on this package cannot have moved regardless: `dist/index.cjs` is byte-identical.
- The derivation's own footer names what sits outside those 56 — 50 artifact-roster families, 11 wide-population families, 5 path-scheduled CI jobs and the always-runs tail. Those are CI's.

Repo-wide `pnpm lint` was not run locally: it is a repo-scale scan CI owns.

## Acceptance notes

- The `errorVariable` description in this file's own action descriptor still reads "a `TryCatchErrorValue`: `nodeId`, `message`, and `iteration` / `item` when the failure happened inside a loop body" — it never listed `code`, before or after this card. That is an incomplete enumeration rather than an instruction that fails when followed, so it is noted here and not filed, and it is deliberately out of this PR's scope: this card's ruling is the smallest correct diff. Whoever next touches `#14419`'s surface in this file is the natural taker.
- The file's own module docblock already describes `code` correctly as bound; it never claimed the key was undeclared, so it needed no edit.
